entities.name: Zika Virus
entities.description: An acute mosquito-borne arboviral disease caused by Zika virus (flavivirus), characterized by a mild self-limiting illness with low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular exanthem, bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, and migratory polyarthralgia, with critical potential for severe neurotropic and teratogenic complications including Guillain-Barré syndrome and Congenital Zika Syndrome.

entities.name: Acute Zika Fever
entities.description: A benign, self-limiting acute systemic viral illness lasting 2 to 7 days characterized by low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular rash, non-purulent conjunctivitis, and migratory polyarthralgia.

entities.name: Asymptomatic Infection
entities.description: Subclinical viral infection without overt symptoms occurring in approximately 75% to 80% of infected immunocompetent individuals who nevertheless develop neutralizing antibodies and can transmit the virus.

entities.name: Congenital Microcephaly
entities.description: Severe neurodevelopmental cranial reduction where infant head circumference is greater than 3 standard deviations below the mean for gestational age and sex, resulting from ZIKV targeting neural progenitor cells.

entities.name: Fetal Ventriculomegaly
entities.description: Pathological enlargement and dilation of the lateral cerebral ventricles occurring ex-vacuo due to massive destruction of fetal periventricular brain parenchyma.

entities.name: Intracranial Calcifications
entities.description: Coarse or punctate mineralized deposits situated characteristically at the corticomedullary junction, basal ganglia, and periventricular zones following dystrophic necrosis of fetal brain tissue.

entities.name: Simplified Gyral Pattern
entities.description: Abnormal cerebral cortical development characterized by pachygyria, lissencephaly, and polymicrogyria secondary to disrupted neurogenesis and impaired neuronal migration.

entities.name: Cerebral Cortical Thinning
entities.description: Marked reduction in cortical thickness and volume caused by premature apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in radial glial and cortical neural progenitor populations.

entities.name: Congenital Arthrogryposis
entities.description: Multiple congenital joint contractures affecting distal extremities (talipes equinovarus, knee and elbow flexion contractures) arising secondary to in utero fetal hypokinesia and spinal motor neuron loss.

entities.name: Chorioretinal Macular Atrophy
entities.description: Ocular congenital lesion featuring focal pigmentary mottling, retinal pigment epithelium atrophy, and sharply demarcated chorioretinal scarring localized to the central macula.

entities.name: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia
entities.description: Underdevelopment and pallor of the optic disc, double-ring sign, and abnormal cup-to-disc ratio resulting in permanent visual impairment in congenital Zika cases.

entities.name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
entities.description: Congenital bilateral or unilateral auditory deficit caused by viral injury to the auditory nerve or cochlear structures in prenatally exposed infants.

entities.name: Fetal Demise
entities.description: In utero death of the developing embryo or fetus across any trimester of gestation precipitated by severe placental insufficiency and disseminated fetal viral infection.

entities.name: Spontaneous Miscarriage
entities.description: Early involuntary termination of pregnancy prior to 20 weeks of gestation triggered by acute syncytiotrophoblast destruction and intense intervillositis.

entities.name: Preterm Birth
entities.description: Delivery of a neonate prior to 37 completed weeks of gestation stimulated by acute intrauterine inflammatory signaling and placental insufficiency.

entities.name: Intrauterine Growth Restriction
entities.description: Pathological reduction in estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age due to compromised uteroplacental vascular perfusion.

entities.name: Fetal Hydrops
entities.description: Severe fetal pathological fluid accumulation in at least two serosal compartments (ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, subcutaneous edema) driven by severe viral infection.

entities.name: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
entities.description: An acute autoimmune post-infectious demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy developing 1 to 3 weeks after acute infection, characterized by ascending flaccid paralysis and areflexia.

entities.name: Ascending Flaccid Paralysis
entities.description: Progressive, symmetrical loss of motor function commencing in the lower extremities and advancing cephalad to involve upper limbs, trunk, and cranial nerves.

entities.name: Acute Transverse Myelitis
entities.description: Focal inflammatory demyelination spanning one or more spinal cord segments presenting with rapidly evolving paraparesis, sensory level deficit, and sphincter dysfunction.

entities.name: Acute Meningoencephalitis
entities.description: Direct invasion and inflammation of meninges and brain parenchyma in adults or children presenting with fever, altered mental status, meningismus, and focal neurological signs.

entities.name: Cranial Nerve Palsy
entities.description: Unilateral or bilateral neuropathy affecting cranial nerves, most commonly peripheral facial nerve (CN VII) palsy and ocular motor paresis (CN III, VI).

entities.name: Acute Flaccid Myelitis
entities.description: Sudden onset of asymmetric or symmetric flaccid limb weakness with diminished reflexes attributed to selective viral inflammation of spinal cord anterior horn cells.

entities.name: Migratory Polyarthralgia
entities.description: Transient, non-erosive joint discomfort shifting between small and medium peripheral joints, notably wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, ankles, and knees.

entities.name: Periarticular Tenosynovitis
entities.description: Inflammation of synovial sheaths surrounding flexor and extensor tendons of the wrist and ankle, causing dorsal hand and foot swelling without joint destruction.

entities.name: Generalized Myalgia
entities.description: Diffuse skeletal muscle pain and soreness commonly localized to the back, calves, and shoulders during the acute viremic phase.

entities.name: Retro-Orbital Pain
entities.description: Mild to moderate dull retrobulbar ache aggravated by lateral or superior eye movement, distinctively milder than the agonizing retro-orbital pain of dengue.

entities.name: Frontal Cephalea
entities.description: Throbbing or dull persistent frontal and holocranial headache presenting as one of the earliest prodromal symptoms.

entities.name: Constitutional Asthenia
entities.description: Profound fatigue, physical exhaustion, and generalized malaise that typically accompanies the acute phase and may linger for 1 to 2 weeks post-defervescence.

entities.name: Transient Anorexia
entities.description: Loss of appetite often accompanied by mild dysgeusia or nausea during the acute febrile and eruptive stages.

entities.name: Autonomic Dysreflexia
entities.description: Hemodynamic instability, fluctuating blood pressures, cardiac arrhythmias, and diaphoresis arising from autonomic neuropathy in post-Zika Guillain-Barré syndrome.

entities.name: Neonatal Dysphagia
entities.description: Severe impairment of sucking and swallowing coordination in neonates with congenital Zika syndrome, leading to aspiration pneumonia and feeding failure.

entities.name: Neonatal Hypertonia
entities.description: Generalized marked muscular rigidity and hyperreflexia appearing in infancy secondary to extensive bilateral corticospinal tract and motor cortex injury.

entities.name: Talipes Equinovarus
entities.description: Congenital clubfoot deformity involving unilateral or bilateral ankle inversion and plantarflection secondary to fetal immobilization and neurogenic muscle imbalance.

entities.name: Infantile Seizures
entities.description: Early-onset intractable epileptic spasms and focal clonic seizures resulting from extensive cortical dysgenesis and subcortical calcifications.

entities.name: Bilateral Facial Diplegia
entities.description: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness presenting with inability to close eyes, smile, or puff cheeks in Guillain-Barré syndrome variants.

entities.name: Peripheral Paresthesias
entities.description: Tingling, prickling, or numbness affecting distal fingers and toes that precedes or accompanies motor weakness in GBS.

entities.name: Diaphragmatic Weakness
entities.description: Respiratory muscle insufficiency and neuromuscular ventilatory failure requiring mechanical ventilation in 15% to 30% of post-Zika GBS cases.

entities.name: Posterior Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Mild to moderate non-tender or minimally tender enlargement of posterior cervical and retroauricular lymph nodes.

entities.name: Mild Diarrhea
entities.description: Transient loose watery stools or abdominal discomfort occurring in a subset of patients during the early viremic phase.

entities.name: Intense Cutaneous Pruritus
entities.description: Severe, distressing itching of the skin associated with the descending maculopapular rash, often disturbing sleep.

entities.name: Low-Grade Fever
entities.description: Core body temperature elevation between 37.5°C and 38.5°C that lacks the high-spiking chills or rigors of dengue or malaria.

entities.name: Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Erythematous, finely morbilliform or papular cutaneous eruption that erupts within the first 24 to 48 hours of illness.

entities.name: Centrifugal Rash Distribution
entities.description: Rapid outward progression of the exanthem starting on the face and neck and spreading downward across the trunk and extremities to the palms and soles.

entities.name: Palmar Erythematous Macules
entities.description: Discrete, non-blanching or blanching pink macules distributed over the palmar surfaces of both hands.

entities.name: Plantar Erythematous Macules
entities.description: Punctate erythematous macular lesions distributed across the plantar aspects of both feet.

entities.name: Bulbar Conjunctival Hyperemia
entities.description: Bilateral diffuse engorgement of superficial scleral and episcleral vessels without purulent exudate or discharge.

entities.name: Palpebral Conjunctival Injection
entities.description: Bilateral vascular congestion of tarsal conjunctival surfaces without pseudomembranes or cobblestoning.

entities.name: Periarticular Hand Puffiness
entities.description: Soft tissue non-pitting edema localized around the dorsum of the hands, metacarpophalangeal joints, and wrists.

entities.name: Periarticular Foot Puffiness
entities.description: Bilateral diffuse swelling around the malleoli, Achilles tendons, and dorsum of feet without true intra-articular effusion.

entities.name: Non-Erosive Joint Tenderness
entities.description: Palpation tenderness over peripheral joint lines without warmth, erythema, bony enlargement, or joint destruction.

entities.name: Preserved Joint Mobility
entities.description: Full or near-full passive and active range of joint motion despite subjective joint soreness, unlike the crippling joint locking of chikungunya.

entities.name: Severe Craniofacial Disproportion
entities.description: Dramatically reduced cranial neurocranium volume contrasting with a normal-sized viscerocranium and facial skeleton in neonates.

entities.name: Redundant Scalp Rugae
entities.description: Exaggerated transverse skin folds and wrinkling on the posterior occipital scalp (cutis gyrata-like) due to rapid collapse of the fetal brain vault.

entities.name: Depressed Cranial Vault
entities.description: Overlapping cranial sutures and prominent occipital bone projection created by loss of brain parenchymal volume in utero.

entities.name: Premature Fontanelle Closure
entities.description: Early or complete synostotic closure of anterior and posterior fontanelles at or shortly after birth in severely affected infants.

entities.name: Infantile Generalized Spasticity
entities.description: Marked bilateral increase in muscle tone with clasp-knife rigidity and sustained ankle clonus in neonates with congenital Zika syndrome.

entities.name: Hyporeflexic Tendon Reflexes
entities.description: Diminished or completely absent deep tendon reflexes (patellar, Achilles, brachioradialis) in patients presenting with post-Zika Guillain-Barré.

entities.name: Ascending Symmetrical Weakness
entities.description: Progressive, bilateral loss of lower limb power (Medical Research Council grade 0-3/5) advancing symmetrically upward.

entities.name: Suboccipital Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Discrete, non-tender, mobile enlargement of lymph nodes located beneath the occipital protuberance.

entities.name: Palpable Posterior Cervical Nodes
entities.description: Palpable enlargement of superficial posterior cervical chain lymph nodes measuring 0.5 to 1.5 cm in diameter.

entities.name: Palatal Mucosal Enanthem
entities.description: Faint erythematous macules or non-hemorrhagic stippling on the soft palate and uvula without ulceration.

entities.name: Brisk Capillary Refill
entities.description: Rapid return of microvascular blood flow (<2 seconds) following digital compression, confirming intact peripheral perfusion.

entities.name: Absence of Ecchymoses
entities.description: Absence of cutaneous purpura, hematomas, or spontaneous subcutaneous bleeding on comprehensive skin examination.

entities.name: Absence of Petechiae
entities.description: Lack of pinpoint microvascular hemorrhagic lesions on flexural surfaces, distinguishing the rash from dengue petechiae.

entities.name: Normal Spleen Palpation
entities.description: Impapable splenic edge beneath the left costal margin during deep inspiration.

entities.name: Normal Hepatic Span
entities.description: Normal liver percussion span (6 to 12 cm) without tender hepatomegaly or Murphy sign on right upper quadrant examination.

entities.name: Clear Pulmonary Auscultation
entities.description: Normal vesicular breath sounds bilaterally without adventitious crackles, wheezing, rhonchi, or pleural friction rubs.

entities.name: Normal Arterial Pressure
entities.description: Normal systolic and diastolic blood pressure with wide pulse pressure (>20 mmHg), ruling out decompensated dengue shock syndrome.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Total peripheral white blood cell count remains within normal reference limits (4,000–10,000/µL) throughout early acute infection.

entities.name: Mild Leukopenia Pattern
entities.description: Peripheral white blood cell count moderately depressed between 3,500 and 5,000/µL without severe neutropenia.

entities.name: Absence of Agranulocytosis
entities.description: Absolute neutrophil count remains well above critical cytopenic thresholds (>1,500/µL), preserving antibacterial defenses.

entities.name: Preserved Platelet Count
entities.description: Platelet count remains above 150,000/µL without spontaneous mucosal hemorrhage or petechiae.

entities.name: Mild Thrombocytopenia Pattern
entities.description: Platelet count moderately decreased between 100,000 and 150,000/µL that promptly normalizes upon defervescence.

entities.name: Stable Hematocrit Concentration
entities.description: Baseline hematocrit remains stable within physiological limits without hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Normal Serum Albumin
entities.description: Serum albumin concentration remains within normal limits (3.5–5.0 g/dL), reflecting intact vascular endothelial barrier function.

entities.name: Mild Transaminase Elevation
entities.description: Serum aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase levels mildly elevated, typically less than twice upper limit of normal.

entities.name: Normal Serum Bilirubin
entities.description: Total serum bilirubin remains under 1.2 mg/dL, ruling out intrahepatic cholestasis or acute hemolysis.

entities.name: Normal Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Serum creatinine remains within baseline limits (<1.2 mg/dL), indicating preserved glomerular filtration.

entities.name: Normal Blood Urea
entities.description: Blood urea nitrogen levels remain normal without prerenal azotemia or dehydration.

entities.name: Mild CRP Elevation
entities.description: C-reactive protein is normal or mildly increased (10–30 mg/L), distinguishing from severe invasive bacterial infections.

entities.name: Negative Blood Smear
entities.description: Light microscopy examination of thick and thin blood films reveals complete absence of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium parasites.

entities.name: Serum ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Reverse transcriptase PCR of acute serum detects ZIKV RNA up to 10 to 11 days post-symptom onset.

entities.name: Urine ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Real-time RT-PCR demonstrates persistent shedding of viral RNA in urine for up to 2 to 3 weeks after onset.

entities.name: Semen ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Detection of viral genome in male seminal fluid by RT-PCR for several months after initial clinical recovery.

entities.name: Saliva ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: RT-PCR identification of ZIKV RNA in oral saliva samples during the acute phase of illness.

entities.name: Amniotic Fluid RT-PCR
entities.description: Molecular detection of viral RNA in amniotic fluid obtained via prenatal diagnostic amniocentesis.

entities.name: ZIKV IgM Seropositivity
entities.description: Specific anti-ZIKV immunoglobulin M antibodies detected via MAC-ELISA starting 3 to 8 days post-onset.

entities.name: PRNT Confirmatory Neutralization
entities.description: Plaque reduction neutralization testing demonstrating at least 4-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against ZIKV compared to DENV.

entities.name: Flavivirus Serologic Cross-Reactivity
entities.description: Broad cross-reactivity observed on IgM and IgG immunoassays in secondary flavivirus infections.

entities.name: Albuminocytological Dissociation
entities.description: CSF analysis demonstrating elevated protein concentration with normal white cell count (<5/µL) in post-Zika GBS.

entities.name: CSF ZIKV Detection
entities.description: Direct identification of viral RNA in cerebrospinal fluid by RT-PCR in cases of meningoencephalitis or myelitis.

entities.name: Thin Gallbladder Wall
entities.description: Bedside gallbladder ultrasound reveals thin wall (<3 mm) without subserosal edema, striations, or pericholecystic fluid.

entities.name: Absence of Ascites
entities.description: Point-of-care abdominal sonography demonstrates no free fluid in Morison pouch, spleno-renal recess, or pelvis.

entities.name: Absence of Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Serial hematocrit determinations show no upward drift or hemoconcentration ≥20% above baseline.

entities.name: Absence of Pleural-Effusion
entities.description: Bedside lung ultrasound demonstrates normal pleural sliding and complete absence of anechoic pleural effusions or B-lines.

entities.name: Normal Pericardial POCUS
entities.description: Subcostal echocardiographic window reveals normal pericardial space without anechoic fluid strip or cardiac tamponade.

entities.name: Subcortical Intracranial Calcifications
entities.description: Non-contrast cranial CT reveals dense punctate calcifications clustered at the corticomedullary junction and basal ganglia.

entities.name: Fetal Ventriculomegaly Ultrasound
entities.description: Obstetric neurosonography demonstrates prominent dilatation of the lateral ventricular atria exceeding 10 mm.

entities.name: Severe Microcephaly Biometry
entities.description: Prenatal ultrasound biometry reveals head circumference falling more than 3 standard deviations below gestational mean.

entities.name: Pachygyria Neuroimaging Pattern
entities.description: Fetal or neonatal brain MRI demonstrates reduced sulcation, shallow sylvian fissures, and pachygyria.

entities.name: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis
entities.description: Neuroimaging reveals hypoplasia or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with colpocephaly.

entities.name: Cerebellar Hypoplasia Neuroimaging
entities.description: Sonography or MRI reveals disproportionately small cerebellar hemispheres and vermis with mega cisterna magna.

entities.name: Fetal Arthrogryposis Ultrasound
entities.description: High-resolution obstetric ultrasound visualizes persistent fixed hyperextension or flexion contractures of the fetal limbs.

entities.name: Fetal Amniotic Microcephaly
entities.description: Prenatal ultrasound reveals collapsed calvarium, overlapping sutures, and scalp cutis rugae in utero.

entities.name: Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy Pattern
entities.description: Electrodiagnostic testing shows prolonged distal motor latencies, slowed conduction velocities, and conduction blocks in GBS.

entities.name: Decreased Motor Conduction
entities.description: Markedly reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes on nerve conduction studies indicative of axonal injury in GBS.

entities.name: Aedes Aegypti Mosquito
entities.description: Primary daytime-biting domestic vector mosquito adapted to human dwellings and artificial water containers.

entities.name: Aedes Albopictus Mosquito
entities.description: Secondary day-biting Asian tiger mosquito capable of transmitting ZIKV in more temperate suburban zones.

entities.name: Diurnal Vector Feeding
entities.description: Daytime biting behavior with peaks of feeding activity during early morning and late afternoon hours.

entities.name: Tropical Americas Endemicity
entities.description: Widespread transmission throughout Latin America and the Caribbean during major pandemic waves.

entities.name: Caribbean Island Exposure
entities.description: Intense local mosquito-borne transmission across Caribbean island nations and territories.

entities.name: Pacific Island Endemicity
entities.description: Major historical epidemic outbreaks documented across Micronesia (Yap Island) and French Polynesia.

entities.name: Southeast Asian Endemicity
entities.description: Endemic baseline transmission and episodic outbreaks across tropical nations of Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan African Endemicity
entities.description: Ancestral enzootic forest cycles and sporadic human infections across Central and West Africa.

entities.name: Unprotected Sexual Contact
entities.description: Venereal human-to-human transmission via vaginal, anal, or oral intercourse without barrier protection.

entities.name: Infectious Seminal Shedding
entities.description: Prolonged presence of infectious viral particles in male semen lasting weeks to months post-recovery.

entities.name: Transplacental Vertical Transmission
entities.description: Direct vertical transmission of virus from infected maternal bloodstream across the placenta to the fetus.

entities.name: First Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Early gestational stage characterized by peak embryonic vulnerability to severe neurodestructive malformations.

entities.name: Second Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Mid-gestational stage where infection leads to cortical dysgenesis, calcifications, and growth restriction.

entities.name: Third Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Late gestational stage where maternal infection may cause placental insufficiency, IUGR, or preterm birth.

entities.name: Contaminated Blood Transfusion
entities.description: Iatrogenic acquisition of virus through infusion of unscreened platelets or packed erythrocytes from a viremic donor.

entities.name: Solid Organ Transplantation
entities.description: Transmission of virus via transplantation of kidneys, liver, or heart harvested from an infected donor.

entities.name: Laboratory Biohazard Exposure
entities.description: Accidental percutaneous needle puncture or mucosal splash in research laboratories handling live ZIKV.

entities.name: Three-To-Fourteen Day Incubation
entities.description: Interval between viral inoculation via mosquito bite or sexual contact and initial symptom manifestation.

entities.name: Typical Incubation Window
entities.description: Most common incubation interval of 3 to 7 days observed in clinical cohort studies.

entities.name: Sylvatic Primate Reservoirs
entities.description: Enzootic transmission maintaining viral reservoirs in wild forest monkeys and arboreal mosquitoes in Africa.

entities.name: International Tropical Traveler
entities.description: Non-immune individuals traveling to regions of active endemic arboviral transmission.

entities.name: Artificial Water Containers
entities.description: Domestic water storage cisterns, unsealed buckets, and discarded tires providing breeding sites for Aedes larvae.

entities.name: Vascular Plasma Leakage
entities.description: Pathological hyperpermeability leading to pleural effusions, ascites, or hemoconcentration with hematocrit rise >=20%.

entities.name: Severe Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Significant elevation of hematocrit >=20% above baseline reflecting acute intravascular volume loss.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count falling below 50,000/µL accompanied by bleeding manifestations.

entities.name: Spontaneous Mucosal Hemorrhage
entities.description: Overt hemorrhagic diathesis such as epistaxis, hematemesis, melena, or gross hematuria.

entities.name: Hypovolemic Circulatory Shock
entities.description: Cardiovascular collapse with narrow pulse pressure (<=20 mmHg), profound hypotension, and delayed refill.

entities.name: Crippling Destructive Arthritis
entities.description: Severe disabling polyarthritis causing extreme joint immobility and inability to ambulate.

entities.name: Incapacitating Morning Stiffness
entities.description: Protracted inflammatory morning stiffness lasting more than 60 minutes indicating severe synovitis.

entities.name: Continuous High-Grade Pyrexia
entities.description: Sustained temperature elevations exceeding 39.5°C to 40.0°C with severe shaking chills.

entities.name: Prolonged Persistent Pyrexia
entities.description: Fever persisting continuously for more than 7 to 10 days.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Exudate
entities.description: Copious yellowish purulent eye discharge, crusting, and matted eyelids.

entities.name: Severe Photophobia
entities.description: Intense ocular pain and intolerance of light suggesting anterior uveitis, keratitis, or measles.

entities.name: Buccal Koplik Spots
entities.description: Pathognomonic pinpoint bluish-white papules on an erythematous base on the buccal mucosa in measles.

entities.name: Prominent Respiratory Coryza
entities.description: Severe paroxysmal coughing, purulent rhinorrhea, and upper airway catarrh.

entities.name: Tender Retroauricular Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Prominent tender lymph node enlargement behind the pinna and base of skull typical of rubella.

entities.name: Malarial Paroxysmal Rigors
entities.description: Periodic paroxysms of severe shaking chills, teeth chattering, and drenching diaphoresis.

entities.name: Slapped-Cheek Facial Rash
entities.description: Confluent bright fiery erythema of bilateral malar cheeks with circumoral pallor seen in parvovirus B19.

entities.name: Centripetal Vesicular Eruption
entities.description: Pruritic vesicular lesions progressing from macules to papules to fluid-filled teardrop blisters in varicella.

entities.name: Hyperbilirubinemic Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, clinical jaundice, and dark urine indicating hepatic failure or biliary stasis.

entities.name: Oliguric Renal Failure
entities.description: Severe reduction in urine output with acute elevation of serum creatinine and urea in Weil disease.

entities.name: Inoculation Cutaneous Eschar
entities.description: Cigarette-burn necrotic skin lesion with surrounding erythematous halo pathognomonic of scrub typhus.

entities.name: Massive Splenomegaly
entities.description: Significant enlargement of the spleen extending well below the left costal margin in visceral leishmaniasis.

entities.name: Severe Agranulocytic Leukopenia
entities.description: Absolute neutrophil count dropping below 500/µL or WBC <2,000/µL indicating severe bone marrow suppression.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus infection presenting with high fever, severe breakbone arthralgia, retro-orbital ache, plasma leakage, and thrombocytopenia.

entities.name: Chikungunya Virus Disease
entities.description: Alphavirus infection presenting with abrupt high fever and crippling symmetrical polyarthritis persisting for months.

entities.name: Yellow Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus illness presenting with toxic phase icterus, hematemesis, oliguria, and high mortality rate.

entities.name: Measles Virus Infection
entities.description: Morbillivirus infection characterized by cough, coryza, photophobic conjunctivitis, high fever, and Koplik spots.

entities.name: Rubella Virus Infection
entities.description: Togavirus causing mild fever, maculopapular rash, and prominent tender suboccipital and postauricular lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Parvovirus B19 Infection
entities.description: Erythrovirus causing slapped-cheek facial rash in children and acute symmetric polyarthritis in adult females.

entities.name: West Nile Encephalitis
entities.description: Flavivirus causing neuroinvasive asymmetric flaccid paralysis, tremor, and parkinsonian features.

entities.name: Mayaro Virus Disease
entities.description: Amazon basin alphavirus presenting with acute fever, disabling chronic polyarthritis, and maculopapular exanthem.

entities.name: Oropouche Fever
entities.description: Orthobunyavirus transmitted by Culicoides midges causing abrupt fever, retro-orbital ache, and frequent symptomatic relapses.

entities.name: Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Protozoan infection causing paroxysmal fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and positive thick film microscopy.

entities.name: Leptospirosis Disease
entities.description: Spirochetal zoonosis causing conjunctival suffusion, intense calf pain, jaundice, and acute oliguric renal failure.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus Infection
entities.description: Orientia infection presenting with necrotic inoculation eschar, high continuous fever, and regional adenopathy.

entities.name: Acute HIV Seroconversion
entities.description: Early retroviral syndrome with high fever, maculopapular rash, oral ulcerations, and generalized adenopathy.

entities.name: Infectious Mononucleosis
entities.description: Epstein-Barr virus illness featuring exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, and atypical lymphocytosis.

entities.name: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
entities.description: Congenital herpesvirus infection causing periventricular calcifications, petechial rash, and sensorineural deafness.

entities.name: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
entities.description: Congenital protozoan disease featuring diffuse intracranial calcifications, obstructive hydrocephalus, and chorioretinitis.

entities.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
entities.description: Congenital togavirus infection featuring cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus.

entities.name: Secondary Syphilis
entities.description: Treponemal spirochete disease causing copper-red papulosquamous rash on palms and soles with condyloma lata.

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents acutely as a mild self-limiting systemic febrile illness lasting 2 to 7 days characterized by low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, non-purulent conjunctivitis, and peripheral polyarthralgia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests subclinically in approximately 75% to 80% of infected human hosts who remain entirely asymptomatic but capable of transmitting the virus through blood or sexual contact.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Causes severe congenital microcephaly in infants exposed in utero, characterized by profound disproportion between cranial vault and facial skeleton due to viral destruction of fetal neural progenitor cells.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as asymmetric or symmetric fetal ventriculomegaly on prenatal imaging, resulting from massive cerebral parenchymal volume loss and white matter destruction.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Leads to dystrophic intracranial calcifications predominantly distributed at the corticomedullary junction and basal ganglia in congenital Zika syndrome.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Causes severe disruption of cerebral cortical development manifesting as a simplified gyral pattern, pachygyria, or lissencephaly on neonatal neuroimaging.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as profound cerebral cortical thinning with reduced neocortical mantle thickness secondary to selective viral tropism for radial glia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Causes congenital arthrogryposis multiplex with severe non-progressive joint contractures resulting from embryonic motor neuron loss and prolonged fetal akinesia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as focal chorioretinal macular atrophy with severe pigmentary mottling and scarring in infants afflicted with congenital Zika syndrome.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Causes optic nerve hypoplasia, optic disc pallor, and coloboma in infants following transplacental fetal viral neuroinvasion.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Results in sensorineural hearing loss in 5% to 10% of infants with congenital Zika syndrome, requiring routine newborn auditory brainstem evoked response screening.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intrauterine fetal demise or stillbirth in pregnant women experiencing acute gestational Zika virus infection.

[EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted by competent secondary vector Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, capable of surviving in temperate and suburban habitats.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired during peak daylight mosquito feeding hours, specifically during early morning and late afternoon hours before dusk.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Linked epidemiologically to residence or travel in endemic tropical regions of South, Central, and North America with active transmission.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired through travel to Caribbean islands and archipelagos harboring widespread established Aedes vector populations.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Linked to travel or residence across Pacific Island nations, including historical epicenter outbreaks on Yap Island and French Polynesia.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Associated with baseline endemic viral circulation and sporadic urban outbreaks across tropical Southeast Asian nations.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Associated with ancestral sylvatic and urban viral lineages across Central and West Africa, where ZIKV was first isolated.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired non-vectorially through unprotected vaginal, anal, or oral intercourse with a partner infected with Zika virus.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted sexually via prolonged shedding of replication-competent infectious virus in human seminal fluid lasting months post-onset.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted hematogenously across the placental syncytiotrophoblast and Hofbauer cells directly into the developing fetal circulation.

[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Poses substantial risk for fetal neurodevelopmental disruption, cerebral calcifications, ventriculomegaly, and growth restriction.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Remains vulnerable to congenital infection, placental insufficiency, preterm labor, and late-onset subtle neurosensory deficits.

[EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted iatrogenically through solid organ transplantation harvested from an actively viremic allograft donor.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired occupationally via accidental percutaneous needle-stick inoculation or mucocutaneous splash in research laboratories.

[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Typically manifests clinical illness within a median incubation window of 3 to 7 days following vector inoculation.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Maintained in African and Asian jungle sylvatic enzootic cycles between arboreal non-human primates and forest canopy Aedes mosquitoes.

[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of objective systemic vascular plasma leakage (pleural effusion, ascites, or hemoconcentration) rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Serial hematocrit increase of 20% or more above baseline rules out uncomplicated Zika virus and strongly indicates severe dengue.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Platelet count dropping below 50,000/µL rules out uncomplicated Zika virus, pointing toward dengue, severe malaria, or leptospirosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of spontaneous bleeding, epistaxis, hematemesis, melena, or menorrhagia rules out uncomplicated Zika in favor of hemorrhagic fevers.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Hypotension, narrow pulse pressure (≤20 mmHg), cold clammy extremities, or oliguria rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Severe, crippling, incapacitating polyarthritis that prevents walking or normal hand grip rules out Zika in favor of Chikungunya.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Severe inflammatory joint stiffness lasting over 1 hour upon waking rules out Zika virus, supporting Chikungunya or autoimmune disease.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Continuous high-grade fever exceeding 39.5°C to 40.0°C rules out the typical low-grade fever profile of Zika virus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Fever persisting beyond 7 to 10 days rules out uncomplicated acute Zika virus, which reliably defervesces within 2 to 7 days.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Copious purulent or mucopurulent ocular discharge and morning eyelid crusting rules out Zika's non-purulent conjunctivitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Agonizing photophobia and ocular pain on light exposure rules out uncomplicated Zika, indicating measles, keratitis, or anterior uveitis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of pathognomonic bluish-white pinpoint Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa definitively rules out Zika virus in favor of measles.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Heavy paroxysmal coughing, severe purulent rhinorrhea, and respiratory distress rules out Zika virus in favor of respiratory pathogens.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Prominent, markedly tender posterior auricular and suboccipital adenopathy rules out Zika virus, favoring acute rubella.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Violent teeth-chattering rigors followed by rapid thermal spikes and drenching sweats rules out Zika virus in favor of malaria.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Confluent fiery erythematous malar facial erythema with circumoral pallor rules out Zika virus, indicating Parvovirus B19.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous lesions progressing from papules to pruritic fluid-filled teardrop vesicles on an erythematous base rules out Zika, indicating varicella.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Scleral icterus, overt clinical jaundice, and dark tea-colored urine rules out uncomplicated Zika, indicating yellow fever or leptospirosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Acute oliguria, severe azotemia, or gross hematuria rules out uncomplicated Zika, pointing toward severe leptospirosis or hantavirus.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of a cigarette-burn black necrotic eschar (tache noire) rules out Zika virus, definitively indicating scrub typhus or rickettsiosis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Palpable moderate-to-massive splenomegaly crossing the midclavicular line rules out Zika virus, pointing toward visceral leishmaniasis or chronic malaria.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Absolute neutrophil count dropping below 500/µL or WBC <2,000/µL rules out uncomplicated Zika virus, suggesting drug toxicity or typhoid.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Dengue Fever, which causes high continuous/biphasic fever (>39°C), agonizing retro-orbital ache, marked leukopenia, profound thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL), and potential plasma leakage shock at defervescence, unlike Zika's mild fever, early rash, and non-purulent conjunctivitis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Chikungunya Virus Disease, which causes abrupt high-spiking fever and incapacitating, severe symmetrical polyarthritis with prominent swelling and morning stiffness that persists for months, whereas Zika causes mild, transient, non-erosive polyarthralgia.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Yellow Fever, which progresses to a severe toxic phase with high fever, jaundice, black vomit (hematemesis), acute kidney injury, and high mortality, contrasting sharply with the benign self-limited course of uncomplicated Zika.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Measles Virus Infection, which is characterized by a prominent catarrhal prodrome with high fever, severe cough, coryza, photophobic conjunctivitis, and pathognomonic buccal Koplik spots, all of which are absent in Zika virus.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Rubella Virus Infection, which features prominent tender suboccipital and postauricular lymphadenopathy and lacks the prominent conjunctival hyperemia, mosquito-borne kinetics, and profound fetal brain parenchymal necrosis seen in Zika.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Parvovirus B19 Infection, which causes classic slapped-cheek erythema in children and acute symmetric polyarthropathy mimicking rheumatoid arthritis in adult females, lacking tropical vector exposure, conjunctival hyperemia, and seminal transmission.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from West Nile Encephalitis, which causes asymmetric acute flaccid poliomyelitis-like paralysis and coarse tremors, contrasting with Zika's symmetrical ascending Guillain-Barré polyradiculoneuropathy and characteristic teratogenic fetal syndrome.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Mayaro Virus Disease, an Amazonian alphavirus that causes high fever and debilitating chronic polyarthritis lasting several months, in contrast to Zika's transient 2 to 7 day mild polyarthralgia and non-purulent conjunctivitis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Oropouche Fever, an orthobunyavirus that presents with high fever, severe headache, photophobia, and frequent debilitating clinical relapses occurring 1 to 2 weeks later, whereas Zika resolves uneventfully without biphasic relapses.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Falciparum Malaria, which presents with cyclical paroxysmal rigors, high fevers, hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and intraerythrocytic rings on blood smear, contrasting with Zika's normal CBC, self-limiting course, and rash.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Leptospirosis Disease, which follows freshwater rodent urine exposure and causes profound conjunctival suffusion without discharge, severe calf tenderness, jaundice, and acute oliguric renal failure (Weil's syndrome), absent in Zika.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Scrub Typhus Infection, which features a pathognomonic necrotic eschar at the chigger bite site, regional lymphadenopathy, high spiking fever, and elevated transaminases that rapidly responds to doxycycline, unlike viral Zika.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Acute HIV Seroconversion, which causes high fever, painful mucocutaneous oral/genital ulcers, exudative pharyngitis, generalized lymphadenopathy, and high viral RNA load, lacking Zika's conjunctival hyperemia and mosquito epidemiology.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Infectious Mononucleosis, which presents with severe exudative tonsillitis, prominent cervical adenopathy, splenomegaly, and atypical lymphocytosis on blood smear, whereas Zika features non-exudative pharynx and no atypical lymphocytosis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection, which typically causes periventricular calcifications, petechiae (blueberry muffin rash), and hepatosplenomegaly, contrasting with Zika's corticomedullary junction calcifications, craniofacial collapse, and arthrogryposis.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Toxoplasmosis, which presents with the classic Sabin tetrad of diffuse parenchymal calcifications, hydrocephalus, and chorioretinitis, whereas Zika causes severe microcephaly, craniosynostotic vault collapse, and simplified gyri.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Rubella Syndrome, which features the Gregg triad of dense cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus, whereas Congenital Zika lacks congenital cardiac structural defects and cataracts.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Secondary Syphilis, which causes widespread copper-red maculopapular lesions on palms and soles, condyloma lata, generalized non-tender adenopathy, and positive treponemal serology, lacking the acute febrile and conjunctival presentation of Zika.
